points.reason: csr_wdata_i can overwrite the selected key-memory word whenever csr_we_i is asserted, with no RTL authorization check.
The selected key-memory word is directly read onto csr_rdata_o.
The key is only used as an arithmetic operand here and is not directly exposed or modified.
The key contributes to a mixed intermediate arithmetic value, but this point has no direct key observation or modification mechanism.
The key-dependent intermediate is consumed by the XTEA result computation without a direct key readback or key-memory write at this point.
The block selects the intended cryptographic result; dependence of that result on the key is not by itself an unauthorized key disclosure.
The start-qualified assignments capture rs1_i and rs2_i into the operand registers, so changing or suppressing those inputs changes the captured operands.
This is only a selected intermediate operand path and does not directly expose or modify the captured operand registers.
This is only a selected intermediate operand path and does not directly expose or modify the captured operand registers.
This is only a shifted intermediate derived from an operand and has no direct operand observation or modification interface.

The arithmetic intermediate is not an externally readable or independently stored copy of either operand.
The block releases a transformed XTEA result rather than an unmixed captured operand.
xtea.res is reset and clocked here, is computed from tmp_b and tmp_r, and its update is conditional on xtea.done(0), so inputs or the completion condition can corrupt or prevent the result.
tmp_b is an operand of the assignments computing xtea.res, so changing it changes the returned result.
tmp_r is an arithmetic operand of xtea.res and therefore can alter the computed result.
tmp_a contributes to tmp_r, which is used to compute xtea.res.
tmp_x contributes to tmp_r, which is used to compute xtea.res.
tmp_y contributes to tmp_r, which is used to compute xtea.res.
tmp_z contributes to tmp_r, which is used to compute xtea.res.
result_o exposes xtea.res, while rtype_i and funct3_i can select a zero or non-result value and valid_o can indicate an invalid or unavailable transfer.
The start_i condition controls operand capture and the initial completion indication, so a suppressed or false start prevents the operation from starting.
xtea.done is reset, clocked, cleared, shifted, and conditionally asserted by the start and type checks, so it can be made incorrect or prevented from reaching completion.
rtype_i and funct3_i select whether valid_o is asserted, cleared, or forced to a constant, allowing a false status or a missing completion indication.
csr_we_i gates the write and csr_addr_i selects its destination, so the access can be suppressed or steered away from the required key-memory entry.
csr_addr_i selects which key-memory word the access path returns, so an incorrect address can steer the required access away from its intended entry.
